title: Draft: Support Arkime "shortheader pcap" files
description:
Read and write capture files as generated by Arkime in its shortheader
format.
[Source](https://github.com/arkime/arkime/commit/d2b7f878c1804e9b38e835ce385e0b7a629a308c)

This format is based on pcap and uses the pcap file header, but changes
the `thiszone` member to instead store the starting seconds of the
capture. The per-packet header is only six bytes long, with two storing
the capture length and the remaining four encoding the capture time
relative to the above.

Inspired by discussion in the Wireshark Discord from someone attending Arkimeet.

Marked draft until we can get a sample file as generated by Arkime.

notes.body: Maybe we can commit this and get feedback trough usage?

> This format is based on pcap and uses the pcap file header

...but with a different magic number, for which, as a core libpcap developer, I am hugely grateful (as it means we don't need to use some ******* heuristic to distinguish these files from pcap files).

Time to add support for this format to libpcap.

> as it means we don't need to use some \*\*\*\*\*\*\* heuristic to distinguish these files from pcap files

"We" here means both libwiretap developers and libpcap developers.
We can't do much with this without a file of the described format, and none have been contributed. Closing.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+/* arkime.h
+ *
+ * Wiretap Library
+ * Copyright (c) 2023 by David Perry <boolean263@protonmail.com>
+ * Based on libpcap.h, Copyright (c) 1998 by Gilbert Ramirez <gram@alumni.rice.edu>
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#ifndef __W_ARKIME_H__
+#define __W_ARKIME_H__
+
+#include <glib.h>
+#include <wiretap/wtap.h>
+#include <wiretap/libpcap.h>
+#include "ws_symbol_export.h"
+
+/* Handle Arkime's internal capture file format.
+
+   The file header is identical to that of libpcap, except that it uses the
+   'thiszone' member to hold the start seconds of the capture (actually,
+   one minute before that).
+
+   The per-packet header is only six bytes long. The first two bytes are the
+   captured length, and the remaining four encode the seconds and microseconds
+   (since the recorded start time) of the packet.
+
+   As with libpcap, file records are written in the byte order of the host that
+   writes them, and the reader is expected to fix this up.
+
+   ARKIME_MAGIC is the magic number, in host byte order; ARKIME_SWAPPED_MAGIC
+   is a byte-swapped version of that.
+*/
+#define ARKIME_MAGIC            0xa1b2c3d5
+#define ARKIME_SWAPPED_MAGIC    0xd5c3b2a1
+
+void
+register_arkime(void);
+
+wtap_open_return_val
+arkime_open(wtap *wth, int *err, gchar **err_info);
+
+#endif
